messages.sync.setupServerPrompt:
# Set up a GPT usage sync server for MAA

Build a persistent GPT usage service for my devices running my-ai-assistant (MAA). Follow the target repository’s conventions and existing stack. For a new project, choose a simple transactional database. Deliver runnable source, migrations, isolated tests, configuration examples without secrets, HTTPS deployment and backup instructions. If deployment details are missing, finish local setup first and list the information needed to deploy. Provide the HTTPS base URL and explain how I can obtain the account sync key securely.

## Account and transport

Store and distribute session IDs, parent relationships, models, UTC times, token counts and source devices. Keep raw records. MAA calculates prices, dates, lineage deduplication and device filters. Sessions and usage may arrive out of order. Do not accept conversation content, tool arguments, paths, pricing or GPT credentials. No OpenAI API calls, session recovery or remote deletion endpoint are needed.

Each account has a persistent spaceId and one active sync key. Provide an authenticated administrative CLI or UI to create, enable and disable accounts and reset keys. Generate keys securely (at least 32 random bytes recommended), store their digests, and show plaintext only on creation or reset. Keep admin credentials separate and registration private. Devices share the account key and have distinct device IDs. Authenticate the space by key, then verify the supplied spaceId. A device ID is only a source identifier. Disabling an account returns 403. A reset invalidates the old key with 401. Preserve its space, epoch and history.

All three endpoints accept Authorization: Bearer <account-sync-key> and Accept: application/json. Push uses Content-Type: application/json. Accept an HTTPS base URL with an optional prefix, e.g. https://sync.example.com/maa. Return JSON directly without redirects, CAPTCHA, cookies, additional headers or a generic response envelope. A reverse proxy can terminate TLS using a trusted certificate. Success is HTTP 200. The client timeout is 40 seconds. Requests and responses are limited to 1 MiB (1048576 uncompressed UTF-8 bytes). Redact credentials, cursors and bodies from application and proxy logs, including cursor query parameters.

spaceId and epoch are persistent strings of 1–256 UTF-8 bytes without control characters. Keep the epoch across restarts and key resets. Change it when data rollback or rebuilding invalidates prior confirmations and cursors. Return 409 for an invalidated epoch.

## Records and hashing

Use camelCase. All record fields are required. Represent nullable fields explicitly as null. Preserve string bytes and case without trimming or Unicode normalization. Reject invalid UTF-8, unpaired surrogates and controls. Use case-sensitive database constraints.

A device has a lowercase 32-hex-character deviceId and a nonblank name of 1–128 UTF-8 bytes. sessionId, non-null forkedFromId and model are nonblank strings of 1–512 UTF-8 bytes. Preserve legacy:<deviceId>:<random-file-id> session IDs verbatim. The unknown model can be "unknown". createdAt and timestampMs are null or UTC Unix millisecond integers from 0 to 8210266876799999. Preserve unknown times.

Token counts are integers from 0 to 9007199254740991. totalUsage is null or five integers in this order: input_tokens, cached_input_tokens, output_tokens, reasoning_output_tokens, total_tokens. inputTokens excludes cache hits. cacheReadTokens is separate. outputTokens already includes reasoning. Preserve cumulative counters as recorded. occurrence is 0–4294967295 and must be zero with cumulative counters. Without counters it distinguishes identical events. Validate raw JSON numbers as unsigned decimal integers. Reject strings, fractions, exponent notation and negative zero. Reject unknown fields in session, usage, Device, WireRecord, RemoteRecord and push requests. Additive outer response fields are allowed if they preserve semantics.

SessionRecord:
~~~json
{"kind":"session","sessionId":"thread-1","forkedFromId":null,"createdAt":1791504000000}
~~~

UsageRecord:
~~~json
{"kind":"usage","sessionId":"thread-1","timestampMs":1791504000000,"model":"gpt-example","inputTokens":80,"cacheReadTokens":20,"outputTokens":10,"totalUsage":[100,20,10,0,110],"occurrence":0}
~~~

Wrap each record as {"recordId":"<64 lowercase hex characters>","record":<record>}. Recompute SHA-256 from the UTF-8 encoding of the canonical array below.
~~~text
[1,"session",sessionId,forkedFromId,createdAt]
[1,"usage",sessionId,timestampMs,model,inputTokens,cacheReadTokens,outputTokens,totalUsage,occurrence]
~~~

Use compact JSON without BOM, whitespace or trailing newline. Encode integers in decimal and null as null. Use standard JSON string escapes for quotes and backslashes. Do not escape slashes or non-ASCII characters. The source device ID is excluded except where already part of a legacy session ID. Hash the array, not the HTTP body, sorted object keys or database JSON.

Cross-language test vectors (each input line followed by its SHA-256):
~~~text
[1,"session","thread-1",null,1791504000000]
fd3127c801e7b05afb5d900c6f091806b8e01e5f64a5b3ce70fe22fba89d5f67

[1,"usage","thread-1",1791504000000,"gpt-example",80,20,10,[100,20,10,0,110],0]
ba432543859b5784bca4c5293c5c41afdb1ba4be71677028f0d664854620df5f

[1,"usage","会话/\"1",null,"模型\\A",1,0,0,null,2]
8301484be9dc31c5b241658355f3e68a5efde92ac2e716a158783cf1974dcb22
~~~

## Endpoints

### GET /api/v1/codex-usage/handshake

Verify the key and return the space, epoch and protocol version. No required query parameters, device registration or protocol header. Test connection calls only this endpoint. Advertise exclude-device-records-v1. Older servers can omit capabilities or return an empty array. Ignore unknown capabilities. Do not include capabilities in push requests.
~~~json
{"protocolVersion":1,"spaceId":"space-example","epoch":"epoch-example","capabilities":["exclude-device-records-v1"]}
~~~

### POST /api/v1/codex-usage/push

At most 500 WireRecords per request, up to 1 MiB. Reject duplicate recordIds within a batch with 400. An empty records array can register or rename a device.
~~~json
{
  "protocolVersion": 1,
  "spaceId": "space-example",
  "epoch": "epoch-example",
  "device": {"deviceId":"aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa","name":"Work computer"},
  "records": [
    {
      "recordId": "fd3127c801e7b05afb5d900c6f091806b8e01e5f64a5b3ce70fe22fba89d5f67",
      "record": {"kind":"session","sessionId":"thread-1","forkedFromId":null,"createdAt":1791504000000}
    },
    {
      "recordId": "ba432543859b5784bca4c5293c5c41afdb1ba4be71677028f0d664854620df5f",
      "record": {"kind":"usage","sessionId":"thread-1","timestampMs":1791504000000,"model":"gpt-example","inputTokens":80,"cacheReadTokens":20,"outputTokens":10,"totalUsage":[100,20,10,0,110],"occurrence":0}
    }
  ]
}
~~~

Success:
~~~json
{
  "spaceId": "space-example",
  "epoch": "epoch-example",
  "acknowledgedIds": [
    "fd3127c801e7b05afb5d900c6f091806b8e01e5f64a5b3ce70fe22fba89d5f67",
    "ba432543859b5784bca4c5293c5c41afdb1ba4be71677028f0d664854620df5f"
  ]
}
~~~

acknowledgedIds must contain exactly every submitted ID once, including existing records, in any order. An empty push returns an empty array. Validate first and commit device, content, sources and changes in one transaction before responding. Roll back the entire batch including device renames on any failure. Use (spaceId,deviceId,recordId) for idempotency under retries, concurrent requests and lost replies. When two devices submit identical content, keep both sources and emit a change for each new source.

### GET /api/v1/codex-usage/changes

Require spaceId and epoch. limit is 1–500, default 500. An absent cursor starts a full download. Cursors are opaque nonempty strings of at most 4096 UTF-8 bytes. Optional excludeDeviceId is 32 lowercase hex characters and filters only records from that device, never device metadata or another source for the same record. Send it only with the advertised capability. Invalid parameters return 400. It is a filter, not authentication.
~~~http
GET /api/v1/codex-usage/changes?spaceId=space-example&epoch=epoch-example&limit=500
Authorization: Bearer <account-sync-key>
Accept: application/json
~~~

Example response (a session can arrive on a later page):
~~~json
{
  "spaceId": "space-example",
  "epoch": "epoch-example",
  "records": [
    {
      "deviceId": "aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa",
      "item": {
        "recordId": "ba432543859b5784bca4c5293c5c41afdb1ba4be71677028f0d664854620df5f",
        "record": {"kind":"usage","sessionId":"thread-1","timestampMs":1791504000000,"model":"gpt-example","inputTokens":80,"cacheReadTokens":20,"outputTokens":10,"totalUsage":[100,20,10,0,110],"occurrence":0}
      }
    }
  ],
  "devices": [{"deviceId":"aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa","name":"Work computer"}],
  "nextCursor": "opaque-checkpoint-token",
  "hasMore": false
}
~~~

Each records item contains deviceId and item; item contains recordId and record. Always return both arrays, a nonempty nextCursor and hasMore, even for an empty final page. A rename-only page may have no records. Without a filter, include the requesting device's records. With a filter an empty intermediate page is valid only if its cursor advances. Clients have independent resumable cursors.

## Storage, pagination and recovery

Persist accounts and key digests, spaces and epochs, devices, immutable content, source relationships and an immutable change stream. Use unique keys (spaceId,recordId), (spaceId,deviceId,recordId) and (spaceId,deviceId). A corrected session record can have the same sessionId but a different hash. Enforce uniqueness transactionally in the database.

Per-space change numbers must advance in visible commit order. Allocate numbers and recheck epoch under a space lock held through commit. A bare auto-increment sequence can commit out of order and skip changes. Preserve integer precision. Emit changes only for new sources or actual device changes and capture the device name at that moment.

1. Capture the maximum committed change number as a fixed upper bound for each round. Start at zero without a cursor or immediately after the previous checkpoint. Intermediate cursors preserve position and upper bound.
2. Scan a continuous prefix up to the bound, at most limit raw changes per page. records.length + devices.length must not exceed limit. The entire serialized response including escaping and cursor must fit in 1 MiB. Defer the next whole entry if needed. Only matching filtered records can be skipped while advancing. Preserve order and historical device names.
3. With more changes inside the bound, return hasMore:true and an advancing cursor. An unfiltered intermediate page must contain data. At the bound, return hasMore:false and a checkpoint. The next round captures a new bound. An empty final page may repeat its checkpoint.
4. Bind cursors to the authenticated space, epoch, position and upper bound using persistent random tokens or signatures. Persist signing material across restarts. Return 409 for invalid or wrong-space cursors. Retain history and keep valid cursors usable without routine expiration.
5. Use a v2 signed cursor for filtered requests and v1 for legacy requests. Bind a filtered cursor to its excludeDeviceId; a changed or omitted filter returns 409. Keep old cursors readable. Filtering can start at an old checkpoint. Finish an old intermediate round with its original filter first.

MAA saves upload confirmations only after validating the entire acknowledgement. Persist downloaded records, devices, cursor and download mode in one transaction. Confirming uploads never advances the download cursor. Allow pages to be read repeatedly. With filtering, first connection, cache clearing and sync reset begin with a complete unfiltered history download before uploading pending local records and downloading filtered changes. Resume an interrupted full download with its original mode and cursor. After an epoch change or invalid cursor, handshake again, clear acknowledgements and cursors, and replay local history. Older servers upload first and download all changes. If a capability disappears, reset only the download cursor and mode. Counts include only received and committed records; recovery and incremental downloads contribute to the same round.

Only locally collected records are uploaded. Document consistent database backup, restore and epoch rotation. Preserve spaces, idempotency relationships, sequence numbers and cursor secrets across restarts. Clearing a client cache is local. Other downloads can restore it. Deleting original Codex logs does not delete server history. Changing the server, key or space isolates local caches. Account suspension and key rotation retain server history. In-flight requests authorized with a valid key may complete.

## Errors and compatibility

Return concise JSON such as {"code":"invalid_request","message":"Invalid sync request"}. Do not disclose request bodies, secrets or stack traces. Use 400 invalid_request for invalid fields, hashes or protocol versions, 401 unauthorized for invalid keys, 403 forbidden for disabled accounts, 409 reset_required for an invalid space, epoch or cursor, 413 payload_too_large for more than 500 records or 1 MiB, 429 rate_limited with Retry-After, and 5xx server_error for temporary failures. MAA retries network errors, timeouts, 429 and 5xx after 5/10/20/30 minutes, capped at 30. A 409 allows one recovery attempt per round. Auth, protocol and response-validation errors pause automatic sync pending configuration changes or manual retry. Preserve v1 fields, accounting, hashes, idempotency and deletion semantics. Incompatible changes require a new protocol version and URL path.

## Acceptance and handoff

Use an isolated database, temporary keys and synthetic records. Test real HTTP endpoints without reading real GPT credentials or session logs. Cover all three hash vectors, Unicode/escaping, boundary integers and byte limits, unknown fields, invalid numbers, oversized requests, empty databases and device registration by empty push. Handshake must not register devices.

Test initial and incremental sync across two devices, two sources for the same content, forks and late ancestors, concurrent replay, lost acknowledgements, batch rollback and database failure. Verify pagination over 500 changes, 1 MiB boundaries, fixed upper bounds under new writes, delayed commits, interrupted requests, server/database restarts, device renames during pagination and repeated identical pushes. Test isolated spaces, revoked keys, disabled accounts, tampered cursors, changed epochs and history recovery after clearing a client cache or deleting original logs. When desktop clients are available, verify the main overview, tray and device filter on both devices.

For the example usage record submitted by A and B, retain two sources. All-device totals must be input 80, cached input 20 and output 10. Filtering by either device must show the event. Preserve otherwise identical events with distinct occurrences when cumulative counters are absent.

Deliver runnable source, dependency locks, migrations, example configuration, tests and actual results, OpenAPI 3.1 JSON, startup, upgrade, backup and restore instructions, HTTPS reverse-proxy configuration and authenticated administration. Protect credentials and persistent database storage. Keep admin endpoints separate from the three sync endpoints and preserve their wire responses through middleware.

Explain how to start the service, create a sync account and obtain its key, enter the same HTTPS URL and key in Settings → GPT usage sync on each machine, choose distinct device identities and names, test the connection, select Done to save and sync, and verify history on the other device. After rotation update the key on all devices. Identify which tests passed and which still need the deployment environment.
